index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure presents a comparative visualization of three distinct architectural configurations for mapping latent variables to generative components, labeled 'Entangled', 'Overcomplete', and 'One-to-one'. The layout is horizontally segmented into three panels, separated by vertical dashed lines, each illustrating a different mapping strategy between a set of generative units (denoted g₁, g₂, g₃) and a set of latent variables (denoted z₁ through z₅). All elements are rendered as circles with thin borders; generative units are outlined in blue and contain blue lowercase italicized labels (g₁, g₂, g₃), while latent variables are outlined in gray and contain black lowercase italicized labels (z₁–z₅). In the 'Entangled' panel on the left, three blue generative units (g₁, g₂, g₃) are positioned above five gray latent variable circles. Only the third latent variable (z₃) is connected via thick dark gray lines to all three generative units, indicating that multiple generators share a single latent variable. The other latent variables (z₁, z₂, z₄, z₅) remain unconnected. In the 'Overcomplete' panel in the center, only one generative unit (g₂) is shown above five latent variables. This single generator is connected via thick dark gray lines to three latent variables: z₂, z₃, and z₄, suggesting that one generator influences multiple latents. The other two latent variables (z₁, z₅) are unconnected. The remaining two generative positions are empty circles, implying potential for additional generators not currently active. In the 'One-to-one' panel on the right, three generative units (g₁, g₂, g₃) are aligned vertically above five latent variables. Each generator is connected via a thick dark gray line to exactly one latent variable: g₁ to z₂, g₂ to z₃, and g₃ to z₄. The first (z₁) and fifth (z₅) latent variables remain unconnected, illustrating a sparse but exclusive mapping where each active generator controls a unique latent variable. The figure uses consistent visual encoding across panels—blue for generators, gray for latents, thick dark gray lines for connections—to emphasize structural differences in how generative components interact with latent space.
